title: Hilbert-family values for a morphism of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $a:A\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme test $T\to B$, use $A_T=T\times_B A$ and its structural projection as in [def-sfb-space-relative-morphism-values]. A Hilbert-family value is a closed subspace $D\subset A_T$ in the sense of [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace] whose structural map $D\to T$ is proper, flat, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; quasi-separated means the relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Use the chartwise and topological properties of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and quasi-compactness of [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. Thus the last three conditions say finite presentation. The inclusion is the arrow of the closed subobject, so isomorphic presentations over $A_T$ are identified. If $A=Z\times_B W$ as in [def-sfb-space-relative-morphism-values], the first and second projections of $D$ are its inclusion followed by the canonical projections to $Z_T$ and $W$ (the latter, together with $D\to T$, determines the projection to $W_T$).
